coverage.found: Rosewood/ebony (CITES Appendix II): exports have been stopped since about 2015-16, so no legal market. Organic exports reached USD 350M in 2025 and SYMABIO claims traceability. coverage.category: 31. Gold comptoirs, gold collectors and artisanal gold groups (country-specific)
coverage.found: Comptoir agréments are issued yearly (resumed 17 Apr 2023). Collectors need a laissez-passer to move gold. Royalties and tax at source are planned with no start date. The Centrale de l'or (COM) is bringing collectors into the legal system (Aug 2026). The BFM buys only from tax-compliant operators.

coverage.category: 32. Central beneficial-ownership register, RCBE (country-specific)
coverage.found: The DGI platform launched around 16 Jun 2026 (date from a vendor and the press). Private entities are covered: companies, cooperatives, associations, NGOs, foundations and GIEs. coverage.category: 34. Private schools and teachers (ONEP / MEN) (country-specific)

coverage.found: Loi 95-017 on tourism; more than 650 licensed guides; the guide licensing process restarted after a gap since 2019. No current licence-renewal or reporting rule found.

coverage.category: 36. LFI 2026 and e-invoicing changes for SMEs (country-specific)
coverage.found: Decree of 2 Jul 2025 makes e-invoicing mandatory for B2B and B2G, phased by size, six months after the central platform launches. LFI 2026: IR-without-VAT option for 200-400M Ar turnover (needs certified accounts); rent deductible only with a lease and invoices; non-profit rate 10% to 20%. Overlaps K01.

coverage.found: The permit reopening in 2026 creates a wave of applicants and permit holders. No gem-collector declaration forms were found.

result.competitor: The filing itself is done on the free DGI e-service platform (RCBE, under E-Service on the DGI site), which needs NIFONLINE validation by the No.1 manager. MDG Services (madagascar-services.com) sells a done-for-you filing. A user guide circulates on Scribd. Searches in French for software, firms and RCBE found no product that manages registers, annual confirmations or change tracking across many clients, and no accounting-software module for it. Not checked: whether the DGI platform allows bulk or accountant (mandataire) filing.
result.duty: Real and in force. The 2024 Initial Finance Act (enacted 22 Dec 2023, in effect Jan 2024) created the duty, according to Mercator. A press summary of the search results also cites arrêté n°11689/2024, but the full lexpress article was not opened. The DGI launched the RCBE platform on about 16 Jun 2026 (newsmada 17 Jun 2026; MDG Services). Who must file: all private-sector legal entities, i.e. commercial and civil companies, cooperatives, GIEs, associations, NGOs and foundations. Sole proprietorships and fully state-owned firms are excluded. Thresholds: 25% of capital or votes, 5% for mining (MDG Services only). Frequency: on creation (with the declaration of existence or within 30 days), every year (Newsmada; Mercator says an annual review), and within 30 days of any change. Penalty (Mercator, secondary source): a MGA 10,000,000 fine, tax-card updates blocked until the entity complies, and joint liability of the entity and its owners. No deadline for existing entities had been published as of Aug 2026. The CGI article and the official DGI text were not found or opened.
result.market: No count of entities that must file was found. A ministry presentation (UN workshop, Nov 2024), citing INSTAT, puts formalised MSMEs at over 250,000, but many of these are sole proprietorships, which are excluded. EDBM registers about 430-445 new companies a quarter (Q3/Q4 2024). Associations and NGOs add more, but their number was not found. A rough guess is tens of thousands of legal entities that must file, many of them dormant or informal.
result.reason: The duty is real and recurring: filing on creation, an annual confirmation, and an update within 30 days of any change. The reported penalty is heavy (MGA 10M fine plus a blocked tax card), and associations, NGOs and cooperatives are covered. Still, filing is free and simple on the DGI portal. The data changes rarely, the deadline for existing entities is not yet set, and willingness to pay in Madagascar is low. The likely value is a one-off catch-up wave plus a light annual reminder. That fits a service add-on for accounting firms better than standalone SaaS. No multi-client tool was found. Mercator is the only source for the penalty, and the decree text was not opened, so the size of the pain is uncertain.

Duty is partly real: comptoirs need annual approval (valid one year, about 30 applicants in 2024, 50M Ar minimum capital, supply-chain data required), and the Mines ministry and COM are pushing collector traceability and inspections (Aug 2026). I could not read Decree 2023-334 (fetch 403), so I could not confirm collector registers, laissez-passer mechanics, fees or penalties. I found no royalty withholding at source for 2026, and a gold levy was reportedly abolished in 2024. I found no private gold-traceability software, but traceability is state-led through COM and the export window (GUE). The buyer set is tiny (tens of comptoirs), informal and politically exposed, and the state likely owns any digital system. Weak willingness to pay and a small market.

The vehicle tax (TVM, 5,000-340,000 Ar) was voted in the 2026 Finance Law, with payment due 15 July 2026. On 11 June 2026 the Finance Ministry suspended it "until further notice". It stays in the amended finance law text but "will not be applied", so there is no live annual duty. The e-tsirika QR technical-visit system (DGSR) is a state platform, and the 2024 articles only announce it. The passenger manifold is a Bianco-backed requirement in Mahajanga (Sept 2026), with no legal text, date or sanctions found. Owner-drivers are low-tech, and the state tools cover the core job. The bundle is fragmented and mostly unconfirmed. No private competitor found, but I ran no dedicated competitor search. Market size not found.

The duty is real. Clove exporters need an annual agrément from the commerce ministry. Conditions are tax compliance, a compliant preparation and storage station, and a Treasury fee receipt. 108 exporters were approved for 2024-25 (38 industrial, 70 artisan). But the state launched the free "Alalana" platform on 26 Sept 2026, a single online entry point for vanilla and clove export agrément applications (AfDB-funded). The core filing job is now done on a free state portal, so the product is largely pre-empted. The buyer group is small and the filing is seasonal. The window also moved (the 2025-26 deadline was extended to 31 Dec 2025). I could not open the articles (403) or the 2026-27 arrêté, so the search snippets are the only evidence. Searches found no private competitor.

The duty is real. CSBF Circular 001/2018 (27 June 2018) requires electronic tele-declaration of periodic statements within 15 days, with MFI-specific deadlines. The source is a third-party aggregator (regalert.today), not the official BFM site, so I could not confirm the text is still in force. I did not verify the Instruction 002-DCR/09 risk-centre duty or the 45-day publication rule. The market is tiny: about 16 licensed MFIs at end-2023, and EAM-Finances lost its licence in January 2026. Supervised MFIs are few, and the CSBF runs its own tele-declaration (BSA) system. I found no vendor either way. Few buyers, low willingness to pay, and a regulator-owned channel make this a weak solo-founder target.

The duty is real but weak for this claim. The reopening (Law 2023-007, in force 2 Feb 2026, gold excluded) is an opportunity to apply, not a recurring mandatory workflow. NewsMada says no new applications are taken for now: about 3,000 old BCMM files go first, and the applicants must update their documents. That contradicts the claim's "first come, first served from now" trigger. Recurring PREA duties exist: 1M Ar per mining square to the FMISC and a CSR plan, but I did not find their frequency or penalties. Filing is paper-based, and I found no software competitor and no e-cadastre. Buyers are mostly informal, so willingness to pay is low. The market size is unverified: 1,650 (ITIE) to 3,000 (BCMM) pending files. This looks like a one-off wave, and a consultant or agent service fits better than software.
